name: CAST-CAPP
summary: An independent cavity dark-matter search installed inside the CAST dipole magnet, targeting a different source population from CAST's solar-axion observations.
detection_principle: Four rectangular cavities combine with matched phases to receive narrowband microwaves from Galactic-axion conversion in a magnetic field.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2022 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for Dark Matter Axions with CAST-CAPP

collaboration.name: CAST-CAPP Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Reported 90% CL axion–photon coupling limits reaching 8×10⁻¹⁴ GeV⁻¹, with no signal found.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
